coverage: Four selected cases documenting changes since January 2025. Not a national inventory. Historical findings reflect source periods; present implementation and legal status need follow-up.

records.title: Rebuild filing-season staffing capacity
records.finding: GAO identified 5,162 filing-season departures within 17,047 employees leaving through these two programs. The filing season itself was largely insulated from the departures.
records.impact: Future return processing, taxpayer correspondence and customer service face staffing risks.
records.next: GAO recommended that IRS incorporate staff losses into its strategic workforce plan and plan to reduce its correspondence backlog.
records.unknown: Departures are not vacancies or a hiring target. The number and occupations to hire, and current recommendation implementation, are not established here.

chart.label: Departures through the two programs · employees

records.roles: Return processing and customer service; a hiring target is not established
records.relation: GAO identifies a risk to future service, not a measured decline caused by these departures.

records.title: Address AI workforce skills gaps
records.metric_label: AI-related staff lost in one IRS group
records.finding: Officials in Research, Applied Analytics and Statistics reported losing 63 staff working full- or part-time on AI. GAO found IRS lacked a plan to address its AI skills gaps.
records.impact: Staff losses threaten the agency’s capacity to support and develop its AI tools.
records.next: GAO called for identifying needed skills and planning how to address the gaps.
records.unknown: 63 is a reported loss in one group, not a required hiring count. The appropriate mix of hiring, training and other responses is not quantified here.

chart.label: Reported AI-related staff loss · RAAS group

records.roles: AI support and development; precise roles and headcount are not established
records.relation: GAO links reductions and unaddressed skills gaps to increased risk for AI efforts.

records.title: Grant terminations disrupted delivery
records.finding: GAO reported 362 terminated DHS grants and approximately $1 billion in associated deobligations.
records.impact: Some disaster mitigation projects were delayed nearly a year. Some grant actions were subsequently reversed.
records.next: GAO recommended incorporating lessons from these disruptions before further grant actions. The report does not prescribe a blanket restoration amount.
records.unknown: A termination is not necessarily the closure of an entire program. Current award status and restoration costs require award-level follow-up.

chart.label: Terminated grants by DHS component · count

records.funding: About $1B deobligated; amount needed to restore services is unknown
records.roles: Staffing requirements not established in this case
records.relation: GAO documents disruption from grant actions. Some actions were reversed; the termination count is historical.

records.title: Foreign assistance awards terminated
records.finding: State data reviewed by GAO showed approximately 6,780 USAID awards terminated out of 7,510. Remaining awards transferred to State management.
records.impact: The change reshaped foreign assistance delivery. GAO also identified incomplete staffing and award data at State.
records.next: GAO recommended stronger decision guidance and data. Decisions about restoring particular services require award-level needs and delivery assessments.
records.unknown: Awards are not individual programs. Historical obligations are not savings or a restoration budget; current award and legal status are not independently verified here.
records.funding: Restoration cost not established; historical obligations are not a rebuilding budget
records.roles: GAO identifies staffing-data gaps at State; required hiring is not quantified
records.relation: The record establishes terminations and transfer of administration, not a quantified service-outcome loss for each award.
